NUMBER 9 OF 2022

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.
II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 24

(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of victim families, communities and/or community organizations in the field of women's and children's protection.

(2) Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:

a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 23, are also authorized to handle victims of violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

1. Region is Sukamara Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sukamara. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus within the Sukamara Regency Government. 5. Women's Empowerment is the effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capabilities and self-concept. 6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and has not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of women's and children's rights. 10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, to the victim. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes related to their lives both directly and indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and willingness of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly met, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition where the material, spiritual and social needs of citizens are met so that they can live decently and develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the State or outside the State. 20. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. PUG focal point is an OPD operator who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender-sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving Region to the region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop normally. 29. Spiritual guidance is a systematic mental recovery effort regarding the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 30. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 31.

Article 30

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 22 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 26

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 22 letter c, is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women victims of violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:

a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. Regional Apparatus that conducts government affairs in the social sector;
b. Regional Apparatus that conducts government affairs in the field of women and child empowerment, and may cooperate with integrated service centers, women crisis centers, or existing social community organizations; or
c. religious institutions and/or organizations.

Article 28

(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. being rejected by family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. being neglected if not placed in a safe house. (5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 33

(1) Social reintegration as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with substitute family members, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed at ensuring that:

a. women victims of violence can resume their social lives; and
b. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Article 25

(1) Health Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 22 letter b, constitutes efforts that include aspects of:

a. promotive;
b. preventive;
c. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.
(2) Health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out comprehensively, accessible 24 (twenty-four) hours at the Regional General Hospital and carried out in accordance with health service standards.
(3) Women victims of violence have the right to free health services for both medical costs, medicolegal and visum et repertum.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 54

(1) The Regional Government is obligated to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every child obtains optimal health status from the womb.

(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:

a. promotional, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services; and
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, child victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substance abuse, child victims of violence and child victims of human trafficking.
(3) The Regional Government, community, family and parents are obligated to make efforts so that children born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 31

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services are aimed at providing assistance and protection to women victims of violence and sanctions with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.

(2) Types of legal aid services include:

a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court trial decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The Regional Government provides legal aid to women victims of violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other gender-sensitive legal assistants.

Article 71

Service efforts carried out by the Regional Government for women victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 20 to Article 33 apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for children victims of acts of violence.

Article 32

(1) Repatriation is aimed at returning women victims of violence to their region of origin.

(2) The repatriation of women victims of violence is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.

CHAPTER IV

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Article 2

The System for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. improve the quality of life of women, children, and the quality of families;
b. increase institutional capacity for women's empowerment and child protection in Sukamara Regency, including the development of gender and child data systems; and
c. provide protection of women's rights and fulfillment of children's rights including special protection for children from various forms of violence and other discriminatory treatment.

Article 20

Paragraph (1)

Sufficiently clear

Paragraph (2)

Letter a

What is meant by gender responsive is that all service personnel must be gender sensitive when exploring problems experienced by victims and be able to empower victims. Letter b

Sufficiently clear

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services to victims must be carried out with respect to victims without differentiating beliefs, values and social status.

Letter d

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the privacy of victims. Every piece of information disclosed in the service delivery process must be kept confidential and known only to people who are relevant in the provision of services. Personnel must communicate this principle to victims. Letter e

What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service personnel must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems. Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter g

What is meant by non-judgmental is that service personnel must ensure that whatever the victim's condition, they will not be judged or condemned.

Letter h

What is meant by respecting the victim's choices and decisions is that the provision of services must be done with the victim's consent, starting from the victim will not be judged or condemned

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the personnel; it must be ensured that victims are served in language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or mentally retarded. For this category of victims, interpreters must also be provided, for example from special school teachers.

Letter j

What is meant by fast and simple is that the provision of services must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with proactive service personnel, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. If victims come on referral from other service providers, the receiving personnel must first read the referral letter; efforts must be made so that victims are not asked repeatedly about the same things related to their identity or case narrative

Letter k

What is meant by empathy, namely the ability to put oneself in the position of others (in this case victims). Thus victims feel accepted, understood and can openly tell their problems

Letter l

What is meant by the fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate.

As stipulated in the Convention on the Rights of the Child and the Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination

Article 6

Letter a

Sufficiently clear

Letter b

What is meant by Gender Justice is fair conditions and treatment of women and men. In order for justice towards women and men to be realized, steps are needed to stop things that politically and socio-culturally can hinder women and men from being able to play a role and enjoy the results of their role.

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 28

(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. being rejected by family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. being neglected if not placed in a safe house. (5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 24

(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of victim families, communities and/or community organizations in the field of women's and children's protection.

(2) Reporting as referred to in paragraph (1) may file complaints:

a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 23, are also authorized to handle victims of violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 30

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 22 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

(2) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.
II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

1. Region is Sukamara Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sukamara. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus within the Sukamara Regency Government. 5. Women's Empowerment is the effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capabilities and self-concept. 6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and has not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of women's and children's rights. 10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, to the victim. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes related to their lives both directly and indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and willingness of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly met, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition where the material, spiritual and social needs of citizens are met so that they can live decently and develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the State or outside the State. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop normally. 29. Spiritual guidance is a systematic mental recovery effort regarding the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 30. (1) Complaints of acts of violence against women may be made by reporters consisting of victim families, communities and/or community organizations in the field of women's and children's protection.

Article 26

(1) Social rehabilitation as referred to in Article 22 letter c, is aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of women victims of violence who experience social dysfunction to be able to carry out their social functions in society properly.

(2) Social rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (1) includes services:

a. counseling;
b. provision of safe houses; and
c. spiritual guidance.
(3) The provision of services as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out by:
a. Regional Apparatus that conducts government affairs in the social sector;

Service efforts carried out by the Regional Government for women victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 20 to Article 33 apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts for children victims of acts of violence.

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in Article 22 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in order to handle cases of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.

Article 25

(1) Health Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 22 letter b, constitutes efforts that include aspects of:

b. preventive;
c. curative; and

(4) Further provisions regarding the procedures for implementing health rehabilitation as referred to in paragraph (3) are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 78

(1) The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of women's and child protection periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

(2) In conducting supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regent may appoint PD in accordance with its duties and functions.

(3) The results of supervision and evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute evaluation material for the policy of women's and child protection programs in the Region.

Article 28

(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. being rejected by family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or

a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 31

(1) Law enforcement and legal aid services are aimed at providing assistance and protection to women victims of violence and sanctions with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.

(2) Types of legal aid services include:

a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office; c. legal aid in the examination process at court; d. legal aid in the court trial decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The Regional Government provides legal aid to women victims of violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3), the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other gender-sensitive legal assistants.

Article 33

(1) Social reintegration as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with substitute family members, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed at ensuring that:

a. women victims of violence can resume their social lives; and
b. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

Letter c

What is meant by equal and respectful relations is that whoever the victim is, the provision of services to victims must be carried out with respect to victims without differentiating beliefs, values and social status.

What is meant by maintaining confidentiality is that services must be provided in a place that guarantees the privacy of victims. What is meant by providing a sense of security and comfort is that service personnel must ensure that victims are in a safe and comfortable state in telling their problems. Letter f

What is meant by respecting individual differences is that each individual must be viewed as unique; each person has a different background, life experience and way of dealing with stress (coping mechanism), so that one victim should not be compared with another victim in any respect.

Letter i

What is meant by being sensitive to the victim's background and condition and using language that is appropriate and understood by the victim is that sometimes victims come from regions or economic, educational and environmental backgrounds that are not the same as the personnel; it must be ensured that victims are served in language understood by the victim. Lately, more and more disabled/difable/disable women have become victims of violence, whether deaf, mute, blind or mentally retarded. What is meant by fast and simple is that the provision of services must be given immediately without delay involving various parties, but with proactive service personnel, victims must be guaranteed to go through everything with a simple process. What is meant by the fulfillment of women's and children's rights is that victims are entitled to respect and full use of their rights to survive, develop, be protected, be free from all forms of discrimination and participate.

c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.

a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

(1) Health Rehabilitation as referred to in Article 22 letter b, constitutes efforts that include aspects of:

a. promotive;
b. preventive;
c. curative; and
d. rehabilitative.

Article 64

(1) Facilitation of the juvenile justice system includes criminal and civil justice.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms are defined as:

1. Region is Sukamara Regency. 2. Regional Government is the Regent as an element of the Regional Government administrator who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 3. Regent is the Regent of Sukamara. 4. Regional Apparatus, hereinafter abbreviated as PD, is the Regional Apparatus within the Sukamara Regency Government. 5. Women's Empowerment is the effort to enable women to obtain access and control over economic, political and cultural resources so that women can manage themselves and increase self-confidence to be able to play a role and actively participate in solving problems, so as to be able to build capabilities and self-concept. 6. Women's Protection is all efforts to guarantee and protect women's rights so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination in the form of preventive, repressive and post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not reached 18 (eighteen) years of age, including a child who is still in the womb and has not married. 9. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of women's and children's rights. 10. Violence is any act that results in or may result in misery or suffering, whether physical, sexual, economic, social, and psychological, to the victim. 11. Children's forum is a forum for children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating children's involvement in decision-making processes and enjoying changes related to their lives both directly and indirectly, which is implemented with the consent and willingness of all children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a Regency that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 13. Neglected child is a child whose needs are not properly met, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social. 14. Social welfare is a condition where the material, spiritual and social needs of citizens are met so that they can live decently and develop themselves so that they can carry out their social functions. 15. Gender Mainstreaming, hereinafter abbreviated as PUG, is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. 16. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 17. Women victims of violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 18. Child victims of violence are children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 19. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer or receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether carried out within the State or outside the State. 20. Complaint Handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against women and children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 21. Social Rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the capacity of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 22. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 23. PUG focal point is an OPD operator who has the ability to carry out gender mainstreaming in their respective work units. 24. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against women and children that is gender-sensitive. 25. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point or from the receiving Region to the region of origin. 26. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 27. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide a sense of security to victims of violence. 28. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children so that they can grow and develop normally. 29. Spiritual guidance is a systematic mental recovery effort regarding the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 30. Gender Responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 31.

Article 33

(1) Social reintegration as referred to in Article 32 paragraph (2) is carried out in order to reunite women victims of violence with substitute family members, or communities that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.

(2) Social reintegration is aimed at ensuring that:

a. women victims of violence can resume their social lives; and
b. women victims of violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after the victim receives social rehabilitation services.

Article 28

(1) The Regional Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.

(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 26 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

(3) The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

(4) The criteria for women victims of violence who require safe houses include:

a. their life is threatened;
b. being rejected by family or community; c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. being neglected if not placed in a safe house. (5) The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.

Article 73

CONCERNING

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT AND CHILD PROTECTION

I. GENERAL

The 1945 Constitution as a constitutional foundation has explicitly regulated the importance of protection of Human Rights, including women's and children's rights. In addition to the guarantee from the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, the guarantee that every person must have the same dignity and degree has also been internationally recognized. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights or UDHR of 1948, which underlies Human Rights in general, has guaranteed that all people are born with freedom, have dignity and equal rights without exception.

The 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia mandates that Regional Governments regulate and manage regional government affairs aimed at realizing community welfare through improved services, protection and empowerment of the community. As a component of society that plays an important role in realizing a quality generation and as successors to the nation's struggle, women and children must receive guarantees for the fulfillment of children's rights.

To ensure the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection in accordance with human dignity and in order to carry out mandatory affairs, regional governments need to provide legal certainty in the implementation of women's empowerment and child protection through the formulation of a policy. The formulation of such policy is a form of support and concrete effort from various other parties in ensuring the fulfillment of women's and children's rights.

The Implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection is carried out based on the principles of:

a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of women and children;
c. the right to life, survival and development; d. respect for children and legal certainty; and
e. local wisdom and justice and gender equality.

The formulation of the Regional Regulation on Women's Empowerment and Child Protection aims to:

a. provide guidance in the planning and implementation of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection policies;
b. increase efforts in Women's Empowerment and fulfillment of children's rights in order to realize improved quality of life for women and children in the Region;
c. increase protection efforts for women and children from actions and policies that violate women's and children's rights; d. increase the value of local wisdom and the role of customs in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, and
e. increase the role of Regional Government and other community institutions in Women's Empowerment and Child Protection efforts.

The Regional Regulation concerning Women and Child Protection regulates:

a. Improving the quality of life for women, which contains government responsibilities, implementation of PUG, efforts to increase the role, quality and capacity of women in the political, legal, social and economic fields;
b. Protection of women, which contains regional government responsibilities in the protection of women, prevention of violence against women, protection for women victims of violence, and complaint handling;
c. Child Protection, which contains regional government, parent/family and community responsibilities in child protection and efforts made by regional governments in implementing child protection. In addition, the need to establish child forums and Child-Friendly Regency as a form of appreciation in realizing protection and fulfillment of children's rights.
